skills.name: Adding and subtracting negative numbers
skills.description: Number-line model for adding and subtracting integers.

INT_TWO_NEG_POS.label: Uses 'two negatives make a positive' when adding
INT_TWO_NEG_POS.explanation: Works out −3 + (−4) as 7, borrowing the multiplication sign rule.

INT_IGNORE_SIGNS.label: Ignores or mixes up the signs when adding
INT_IGNORE_SIGNS.explanation: Works out −5 + 3 as 8, −8 or 2 instead of −2.

INT_SUB_NEG.label: Thinks subtracting a negative number makes the answer smaller

INT_MUL_SIGN.label: Gets the sign wrong when multiplying negative numbers

adding_integers.title: Adding and subtracting negative numbers
adding_integers.big_idea: On a number line, adding a negative number moves you left. Two negatives added together make a MORE negative number. 'Two negatives make a positive' is a rule for multiplying, not adding.
steps: Find the first number on the number line.
Adding a positive number: move right. Adding a negative number: move left.
Subtracting a negative number is the same as adding its positive: 7 − (−2) = 7 + 2.
adding_integers.sense_check: If you owe ₹3 and borrow ₹4 more, you owe ₹7: −3 + (−4) = −7, not +7.

multiplying_integers.title: Multiplying negative numbers
multiplying_integers.big_idea: Multiply the sizes, then use the sign rule: same signs give a positive answer, different signs give a negative answer.
steps: Ignore the signs and multiply the sizes.
Look at the signs: both negative, or both positive, gives a positive answer.
One negative and one positive gives a negative answer.
Write the sign in front of your answer.
multiplying_integers.sense_check: 3 × (−4) means three lots of −4: −4 −4 −4 = −12. So positive × negative is negative.
